items.question:
Write a précis of the following passage in about 100 words and give it a suitable title.

"Technology has transformed the way we live, work and communicate. A generation ago, a letter took days to reach a distant relative; today a message crosses continents in a second. Farmers who once depended on the word of a local trader can now check crop prices on a mobile phone, and students in remote villages can watch lessons taught by the finest teachers. Banking, ticketing and even seeing a doctor have moved online, saving time and travel for millions. Yet these gains carry a shadow. The same devices that connect us can isolate us, as people scroll alone instead of talking. Endless notifications fracture our attention and make deep, patient thought harder. Children exposed to screens too early may struggle with sleep and social skills, and the flood of unverified information online spreads rumours as quickly as facts. Technology, in short, is neither a blessing nor a curse in itself; its value depends entirely on how wisely we choose to use it. Used with discipline and purpose, it can free time and widen opportunity; used carelessly, it can waste both. The task before us is not to reject technology but to master it."
items.modelAnswer:
**Title: Using Technology Wisely**

**Model précis (≈100 words):**

Technology has changed how we live, work and communicate. Messages now cross the world instantly; farmers check prices, village students learn from top teachers, and banking, ticketing and medical advice have moved online, saving time for millions. These benefits, however, have a darker side. The same devices can isolate people, fracture attention and make deep thought harder; early screen use can harm children's sleep and social skills, and unverified information spreads rumours fast. Technology is neither blessing nor curse in itself — its worth depends on how wisely it is used. The need is not to reject it but to master it.

**Marking scheme (15 marks)**

| Criterion | Marks |
|---|---|
| Central idea captured (value depends on wise use) | 4 |
| All main points, none added (benefits + harms + conclusion) | 4 |
| Correct length (~100 words) and single paragraph | 2 |
| Own words, reported/third-person form | 2 |
| Suitable title | 1 |
| Grammar and flow | 2 |

**Examiner notes:** The passage is ~200 words here; the précis target is one-third of the given length. Penalise any added opinion, copied full sentences, or a missing side of the argument (benefits OR harms).
keyPoints: Central idea = technology's value depends on how wisely it is used; neither blessing nor curse.
Benefits to keep: instant communication, crop prices, remote learning, online banking/ticketing/health.
Harms to keep: isolation, fractured attention, harm to children, spread of unverified information.
Conclusion to keep: master technology, do not reject it.
Marks reward central idea, all main points, correct length, own words, title, grammar.
items.source: SSC-standard précis practice passage (original); APPSC 07/2026 English syllabus — Précis Writing.

items.question:
Translate the following Telugu passage into English, keeping the meaning, tense and register faithful.

"మా ఊరిలో ప్రతి సంవత్సరం సంక్రాంతి పండుగను ఎంతో వైభవంగా జరుపుకుంటారు. ఇళ్ల ముందు రంగవల్లులు వేస్తారు, గొబ్బెమ్మలు పెడతారు. పిల్లలు కొత్త బట్టలు ధరించి సంతోషంగా ఆడుకుంటారు. రైతులు తమ పంట చేతికి వచ్చినందుకు దేవునికి కృతజ్ఞతలు తెలుపుతారు. బంధువులందరూ కలిసి భోజనం చేస్తారు. ఈ పండుగ మనకు కుటుంబ ప్రేమను, కష్టపడే స్వభావాన్ని గుర్తు చేస్తుంది."
(gloss: In our village, the Sankranti festival is celebrated grandly every year; rangoli is drawn and gobbemma placed before houses; children wear new clothes and play happily; farmers thank God for the harvest; all the relatives eat together; the festival reminds us of family love and the value of hard work.)
items.modelAnswer:
**Model translation:**

In our village, the Sankranti festival is celebrated with great splendour every year. People draw rangoli (colourful floor patterns) in front of their houses and place *gobbemma* (decorated dung-flower mounds) on them. Children put on new clothes and play happily. Farmers offer thanks to God for the harvest they have gathered. All the relatives come together and share a meal. This festival reminds us of the love within a family and the value of hard work.

**Notes on choices:**
- 'సంక్రాంతి' and '*gobbemma*' are **retained and briefly glossed** — culture-specific terms are not replaced by Western equivalents.
- Telugu **SOV order** is reordered into English **SVO** ('celebrated ... every year', 'draw rangoli ... in front of their houses').
- The **present habitual tense** of the original is preserved throughout.

**Marking scheme (15 marks)**

| Criterion | Marks |
|---|---|
| Fidelity of meaning — no addition or omission | 6 |
| Correct English grammar and natural SVO word order | 4 |
| Register/tone preserved (festive, descriptive) | 2 |
| Culture terms & names handled well (retain + gloss) | 2 |
| Spelling and punctuation | 1 |

**Examiner notes:** Do not penalise a candidate who translates 'gobbemma' with a short description rather than the exact term. Penalise substituting an unrelated festival, dropping the 'family love / hard work' moral, or leaving Telugu SOV order uncorrected.
keyPoints: Translate sense-for-sense; retain Sankranti/gobbemma with a brief gloss, never a Western swap.
Reorder Telugu SOV into English SVO and add English articles.
Preserve the present habitual tense and the festive, descriptive register.
Keep every point, including the closing moral (family love and value of hard work).
Marks weight fidelity of meaning highest, then grammar/word order, then register and culture terms.
items.source: SSC-standard translation practice (original Telugu passage); APPSC 07/2026 English syllabus — Translation.

items.question:
Write a précis of the following passage in about 90 words and give it a suitable title.

"Reading is among the most rewarding of human habits, yet it is quietly disappearing in an age of screens. A book asks for patience: it cannot be skimmed like a feed or paused like a video without loss. In return, it offers what little else can — the slow, deep attention in which real understanding grows. Through reading we live many lives, travel to distant times and places, and meet minds far removed from our own; in doing so we learn empathy, for to follow another's story is to feel, briefly, as they feel. Reading also builds the vocabulary and clarity of thought on which good writing and speech depend. Children who read early tend to do better across every subject, not because reading is a subject itself, but because it is the tool with which all other learning is done. The danger today is not that books will vanish, but that we will forget how to give them the unhurried attention they need. To keep reading alive is therefore to protect a habit of mind — the capacity for patience, imagination and independent thought — that no device can supply."
items.modelAnswer:
**Title: The Enduring Value of Reading**

**Model précis (≈90 words):**

Reading, an old and rewarding habit, is fading in the screen age because it demands the patience that skimming and videos discourage. Yet it repays this with deep attention and understanding, lets us share other lives and so builds empathy, and strengthens vocabulary and clear thought. Early readers do better in every subject, since reading is the tool of all learning. The real risk is not that books will disappear but that we will stop giving them unhurried attention. Protecting reading means protecting patience, imagination and independent thought that no device provides.

**Marking scheme (15 marks)**

| Criterion | Marks |
|---|---|
| Central idea captured (reading protects deep attention/thought) | 4 |
| All main points, none added (empathy, vocabulary, learning tool, the danger) | 4 |
| Correct length (~one-third, ~90 words), single paragraph | 2 |
| Own words, reported/third-person form | 2 |
| Suitable title | 1 |
| Grammar and flow | 2 |

**Examiner notes:** This is a summary at about one-third length. Penalise copied sentences, an added opinion, or dropping a main point (e.g. empathy or the closing danger).
keyPoints: Central idea = reading protects deep attention, empathy and independent thought against the screen age.
Main points to keep: patience/deep attention, empathy, vocabulary/clear thought, reading as the tool of learning, the danger of lost attention.
Précis ≈ one-third length (~90 words), one connected paragraph, with a title.
Own words, reported speech, third person; no copied sentences or added opinion.
A précis is a faithful summary — smaller but the same picture.
items.source: SSC-standard précis practice passage (original); APPSC 07/2026 English syllabus — Précis Writing (Item 07).

items.question:
Write a précis of the following passage in about 90 words and give it a suitable title.

"Time is the one resource shared equally by all yet valued by few. Every person, rich or poor, receives the same twenty-four hours a day, but what separates the successful from the rest is how those hours are spent. Time, unlike money, cannot be saved for later or earned back once lost; a wasted hour is gone forever. This is why the disciplined treat time as precious, planning their days, finishing tasks promptly, and refusing to let idleness or endless distraction steal their most limited asset. Yet using time well does not mean filling every minute with work. Rest, reflection and time given freely to family and friends are not waste but investment; they renew the mind and give labour its purpose. The art of living well, then, lies in balance — in spending time deliberately rather than letting it drain away unnoticed. Those who master this art find that they accomplish more and worry less, while those who ignore it are forever busy yet strangely empty-handed. To respect time is, in the end, to respect life itself."
items.modelAnswer:
**Title: The Value of Time**

**Model précis (≈90 words):**

Time is shared equally by all but valued by few; everyone gets the same hours, and success depends on how they are used. Unlike money, time cannot be saved or regained, so the disciplined plan their days and resist distraction. Yet using time well is not constant work: rest and time with others renew the mind and give effort purpose. The art of living lies in balance — spending time deliberately, not letting it drain away. Those who master this achieve more and worry less; to respect time is to respect life itself.

**Marking scheme (15 marks)**

| Criterion | Marks |
|---|---|
| Central idea captured (spend time deliberately; balance) | 4 |
| All main points, none added (equal to all, irrecoverable, balance/rest, outcome) | 4 |
| Correct length (~one-third, ~90 words), single paragraph | 2 |
| Own words, reported/third-person form | 2 |
| Suitable title | 1 |
| Grammar and flow | 2 |

**Examiner notes:** A good summary keeps both sides — discipline AND the value of rest/balance. Penalise dropping the balance point or copying whole sentences.
keyPoints: Central idea = time is equal to all but irrecoverable; live by spending it deliberately and in balance.
Main points: equal hours for all, time cannot be saved/regained, discipline vs distraction, rest/balance as investment, the outcome.
Précis ≈ one-third length (~90 words), single paragraph, with a title.
Own words, reported speech, third person; keep both discipline and balance points.
Do not add opinion or copy sentences; keep the original meaning.
items.source: SSC-standard précis practice passage (original); APPSC 07/2026 English syllabus — Précis Writing (Item 07).
